claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is an as-cast, single-phase BCC dendritic alloy.
The baseline yield strength is 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline compressive strength at 30% strain is 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Mechanical alloying with 0.5 vol% Y2O3 followed by HIP is the proposed intervention.
The intervention will produce a uniform dispersion of 10–50 nm Y2O3 particles within the BCC matrix and along grain boundaries.
The intervention will result in an average grain size of approximately 1 µm.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will strengthen the alloy through Orowan strengthening.
Y2O3 particles will Zener-pin grain boundaries and reduce grain growth at high temperature.
The oxide dispersion will elevate the critical stress for dislocation bypass at 1273 K.
Y2O3 dispersion will increase compressive yield strength at 1273 K by at least 30% relative to the as-cast state.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength of at least 430–450 MPa at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will have a compressive strength of at least 550 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
The prediction applies at 1273 K ± 25 K, a strain rate near 1×10^-4 s^-1, compression to 30% true strain, and an inert or vacuum environment.
The effectiveness of the intervention depends on obtaining a uniform oxide dispersion and avoiding agglomeration or coarsening during HIP and high-temperature exposure.
